clue.text: 'Smack' in Greek is 'skampili'

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A language note claiming the Greek word for a smack is 'skampili'.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a translation, but 'in' points into the letters of Greek is 'skampili', spanning the end of Greek, all of is and the start of the quoted word.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a loud kiss on the lips, the sense behind calling a kiss a smacker.

clue.text: Aquatic creature apt to play around yard in addition to going outside

indicators.note: going outside has the word for in addition to wrap round everything else

parts.note: plus means in addition

indicators.note: around has the shuffled letters wrap round the abbreviation for yard
to play suggests the letters of apt being moved about freely

explanation.surface: An animal suited to playing about in a yard, and also to going out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two wrappers: 'around' works on the shuffled apt and yard, then 'going outside' puts the in addition word round the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is a semi-aquatic Australian mammal that hunts underwater in rivers.

clue.text: Buy and eat fresh peach

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopping instruction: get a ripe peach and eat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' looks like the fruit, but here it is the informal word for a lovely thing or person; 'fresh' scrambles BUY and EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a peach is informal praise for a particularly fine or attractive example.

clue.text: Dicky's exempt from ordinary jurisdiction

definitions.meaning: dicky is British informal for unwell or unsound, as in feeling a bit off
a church or parish described this way is outside the bishop's authority, a technical ecclesiastical sense

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky has been excused from the normal courts.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name; it is the British adjective for slightly ill, and feeling peculiar means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: feeling unwell or odd, and the church-law term for a jurisdiction answering directly to the Crown or archbishop.

clue.text: Vincent possibly accepts knight as royalty

indicators.note: accepts means the actor's surname takes the knight inside it

parts.note: Vincent Price was a horror-film actor, so his surname is one Vincent
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Someone called Vincent takes on a knight and gains royal status.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a male member of a royal family, so one instance of royalty.

clue.text: Took a stimulant, being exhausted

definitions.meaning: to use is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: Someone took a pick-me-up because they were worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both taking drugs and being spent or worn out, as in used-up supplies.

clue.text: Slip, perhaps, if turning round tree

indicators.note: turning round has the two letters of if read backwards

parts.note: an elder is a small tree

explanation.surface: Reads like a slip of the foot when going round a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper; 'turning round' is a single reversal signal, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the slips are close catchers, each an example of a player in the fielding side.

clue.text: For every reversal, stand up and go through it again!

indicators.note: reversal says the Latin word for every is read backwards

parts.note: per means for every, as in per head
to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: A drill instruction: every time you turn, stand and repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprise a piece or role is to perform it once more, a repeat performance.

clue.text: Listen, Do You Want To Know A Secret? (pop song with some terrific leads)

definitions.text: Listen, Do You Want To Know A Secret?

indicators.note: leads are the front letters of the words pop song some terrific

explanation.surface: A pitch for a Beatles single, Do You Want To Know A Secret?, with terrific lead vocals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles' song title reads as a whispered offer of gossip, which is the definition, with Listen before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is the hushed sound used to catch someone's attention before sharing gossip.

clue.text: Late but no one cares

parts.note: late can mean dead, and a death nobody grieves over fits the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Late reads as tardy and nobody minding; in the sense of deceased, it describes someone whose passing nobody mourns.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone departed whom nobody grieves for is said to have gone without lament.

clue.text: Bust might end around top of leg or between knee and ankle!

indicators.note: around has the scrambled letters wrap the single letter taken from leg
bust means broken, so the letters of might end are rearranged
top of picks out the first letter of leg

explanation.surface: A dressmaking warning: a bust measurement might end up anywhere around the leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like the body part but signals an anagram of MIGHT END, and 'around' wraps that round L from 'top of' leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt or coat of this cut has a hem that falls on the calf, roughly halfway down the lower leg.

clue.text: Jolly nasty female replacing king with prince

indicators.note: replacing says the letter for king is swapped out of the word for nasty female
with names the letter for prince that takes the king's place

parts.note: a harpy is a nasty, grasping woman, after the winged monsters of myth
R stands for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A cheerful but unpleasant woman usurping a king in favour of a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly and its synonym both describe a cheerful, contented mood.

clue.text: The philosopher and the man come together

parts.note: he refers to the man
to gel is to come together or set

explanation.surface: A thinker and a fellow joining forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was the German thinker behind the dialectic.

clue.text: One has to stand by Washington in restrained approach to the house

indicators.note: in puts the combined pieces within the word for restrained

parts.note: dry wit is restrained, understated

indicators.note: to stand by means the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: I've is a contraction of one (I) has
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington State

explanation.surface: Someone has to wait beside Washington, quietly, outside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the contraction for 'One has' is ignored, as crosswords always ignore punctuation in entries.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is the private road leading from the street up to a home.

clue.text: Trying to get more behind?

definitions.meaning: to be trying to get it
aft means behind, so its comparative form means further behind, a whimsical reading

explanation.surface: Someone wants more from their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as aft plus -er, the answer is 'more aft', i.e. further back: the question mark flags this playful comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Being after a prize means pursuing it, and the word also means later or to the rear.

clue.text: Gets on and leaves top off

indicators.note: top off removes the first letter of the word for leaves

parts.note: pages are the leaves of a book

explanation.surface: Someone starts out and then departs with a hat removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' is a noun, sheets of a book, not a verb; 'top off' drops the P of PAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on is to grow older, which is exactly what someone does who ages.

clue.text: MacGregors' leader plunged into burn for cover

indicators.note: plunged into puts the leading letter inside the word for burn

parts.note: to sear is to burn

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of MacGregors'

explanation.surface: The head of a Scottish clan dived into a stream for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is a Scottish stream, fitting MacGregors, but here it means scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear a surface is to spread a coating over it, so to cover it thinly.

clue.text: Like salt, for instance, covering one battered roll

indicators.note: covering has the word for for instance wrap round the other pieces

parts.note: say means for instance
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters of roll are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cooking note: like salt, sprinkled over a battered roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is the seasoning in the surface but an old sailor in the definition; 'battered' sounds like cooking but scrambles roll.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a veteran seaman, so behaving like one is seamanlike.

clue.text: Block and (in Paris) street surrounding it

indicators.note: surrounding has the abbreviation for street wrapped round the French word

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: A city block in Paris with a street running all round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is a rectangular paving stone, a block used for laying roads.

clue.text: Shows no character when depressed

parts.note: a keyboard key that, pressed down, prints only a blank rather than a letter

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as a gloomy person lacking personality; character means a typed symbol and depressed means pushed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the long key at the keyboard's bottom inserts a blank gap, not a visible symbol.

clue.text: Unconscious after dropping off front of ledge, losing blood externally?

indicators.note: externally means the word for losing blood sits outside the other piece

parts.note: a wound seeping is slowly losing blood

indicators.note: front of picks out the first letter of ledge

explanation.surface: Someone fell off a ledge and is out cold, bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' reads as a fall from the ledge but belongs to the definition: nodding off. SEEPING goes round L from 'front of' ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Once someone has nodded off, they are out to the world in slumber.

clue.text: Conclusion: don't start improving

indicators.note: don't start means the word for improving loses its first letter

parts.note: mending means improving, getting better

explanation.surface: A grumpy verdict: forget about starting to get better.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of a story is its finish or final part.

clue.text: Faculty fellow has secluded place

parts.note: a lair is an animal's hidden den, a secluded place

explanation.surface: A university department member has a private hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Faculty and fellow suggest a university, but faculty means a natural aptitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty for something is a natural talent for it, the same as a knack.

clue.text: Hide line crease

parts.note: an animal's hide is its fur
a row is a line

explanation.definitionFit: A furrow is a groove or wrinkle, as on a brow, so a crease.

clue.text: She's accepted responsibility for a minor crack (the dorm's affected)

definitions.text: She's accepted responsibility for a minor

parts.note: to have a crack is to have a go

indicators.note: affected means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman takes charge of a youngster after a break-in that hit the dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of dorm's stands for 'is', a link word, so only the dorm and 'the' are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening a sponsor promises to oversee a child's religious upbringing.

clue.text: Break free eventually and look amazed?

parts.note: a gap is a break

indicators.note: eventually points to the final letter of free

explanation.surface: Someone finally breaks loose and stares in wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare open-mouthed in astonishment is what someone does when stunned.

clue.text: Hack's first letter goes on record

indicators.note: first letter goes means the word for hack loses its opening letter

parts.note: to sever is to hack off

explanation.surface: A journalist's first letter is published.
explanation.walkthrough: A hack looks like a journalist and record like a file; hack means cut, and 'on record' is as in the hottest day ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The best ever and the best on record mean the same: of all time measured.

clue.text: Carve the rocks around cave's entrance

indicators.note: around has the shaken letters wrap round the single letter from cave's
rocks means shakes up, so the letters of the are rearranged
entrance picks out the first letter of cave's

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut into the rocks near the mouth of a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' is a verb signalling an anagram of THE, not stone; 'around' puts that round C.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a surface, a form of engraving.

clue.text: It turns plug when new drive head is inserted

indicators.note: is inserted puts the pieces inside the word for plug

parts.note: a spile is a wooden plug or bung

indicators.note: head picks out the first letter of drive

explanation.surface: Something rotates once a new drive head is plugged in.
explanation.walkthrough: A spile is a peg plugging a cask's vent hole; N and D go into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spindle is a rod or pin that rotates, as on a spinning wheel or lathe.

clue.text: Snout stuck in pipe?

definitions.meaning: snout is British prison slang for ...
what gets packed into a pipe bowl, a cryptic hint

explanation.surface: A nose wedged inside a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Snout reads as a nose, but in British slang it means tobacco or a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe smokers pack dried leaf into the bowl, and prison slang calls that leaf snout.
